obligations.summary: Providers established in third countries must appoint, by written mandate, an authorised representative established in the Union before making their high-risk AI systems available on the Union market.
The provider must enable its authorised representative to perform all tasks specified in the mandate.

The authorised representative must perform the tasks specified in the mandate received from the provider and provide a copy of the mandate to market surveillance authorities upon request in an official Union language.

The authorised representative must verify that the EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation have been drawn up and that an appropriate conformity assessment procedure has been carried out by the provider.

The authorised representative must keep at the disposal of competent authorities, for 10 years after the high-risk AI system is placed on the market or put into service, the provider's contact details, a copy of the EU declaration of conformity, the technical documentation, and any notified body certificate.

The authorised representative must provide competent authorities, upon reasoned request, with all information and documentation necessary to demonstrate the high-risk AI system's conformity with requirements, including access to automatically generated logs to the extent under the provider's control.
exceptions: Access to logs is limited to those under the control of the provider

obligations.summary: The authorised representative must cooperate with competent authorities, upon reasoned request, in any action taken in relation to the high-risk AI system, particularly to reduce and mitigate risks posed by the system.

The authorised representative must, where applicable, comply with registration obligations or ensure the correctness of the required information in Annex VIII Section A if registration is carried out by the provider itself.
exceptions: Obligation applies only where registration is required; if provider registers directly, the authorised representative need only ensure accuracy of information

obligations.summary: The authorised representative must terminate the mandate and immediately inform the relevant market surveillance authority and, where applicable, the relevant notified body if it considers or has reason to consider the provider is acting contrary to its obligations under the Regulation.
